sentences.text: Tholodus is a reptile belonging to the class Sauropsida and the order Ichthyosauria.
It is classified within the family Omphalosauridae, which serves as its parent group.
The genus was first named by Christian Erich Hermann von Meyer in 1851, with Tholodus schmidi designated as the type species.
Most specimens were collected from the Ladinian-aged Muschelkalk in Germany, mainly from the Jena Formation where the holotype—the specimen the species is based on—was discovered.
The humerus of Tholodus resembles that of immature individuals of the Asian genus Chaohusaurus, suggesting possible affinities to Grippidia.
This animal lived during the Middle Triassic, specifically from the mid-late Anisian to the late Ladinian stage.
Fossils have been found in Germany, northeastern Italy, and possibly China, indicating a range across what is now Europe.
According to Maisch (2010), the only difference between Tholodus and Xinminosaurus is that Tholodus specimens are on average twice as large as the Xinminosaurus holotype.
